result.summary:
The script is written, runs from the repository root in 103 seconds on one thread with a peak of 1.45 to 1.53 GB, and reproduces every target except two Wilcoxon p-values. Two runs of the finished script (md5 c11e3c99f8dcd8a3a4f45447a324f9b5, 725 lines) gave byte-identical CSV files.

The two departures are a matter of method. The issue text quotes p = 0.007 (all libraries) and 0.012 (without zr3534_4), which are normal approximations; the exact test gives 0.005 and 0.010. The same paragraph quotes the exact value for the heat cohort (0.008), so it mixed the two methods. The script writes both for every comparison.

Three findings go beyond the targets and change how I-09 should read:
- **Cohort is associated with the excess.** The Fisher test on the 13 carriers gives p = 0.19, as in the issue. Under a stricter rule (all 54 CpGs at the cutoff: 1 of 10 heat, 8 of 12 control) it gives p = 0.012. As a continuous quantity the excess is larger in the control cohort (median 19.9 against 4.4 times the library median, exact Wilcoxon p = 0.009; block over flanks 20.7 against 3.6, p = 0.014). Ploidy shows nothing (p = 0.39, 1, 0.56, 0.70).
- **The excess is in every library.** All 22 have more coverage in the block than in its flanks (1.31 to 32 times); the 9 "without the excess" are at 1.31 to 4.83.
- **The block is not simply single-copy.** Counting all 3,570 30-mers, 2,471 (69.2%) occur once and 874 exactly twice. Of the second copies, 868 lie in three places on other linkage groups, none of which reaches the cutoff in any library. The last 113 bases of the block occur 11 to 61 times in the reference.

The script also checks its inputs against each other and stops on any mismatch. It recomputes each library's median, cutoff and number of CpGs at the cutoff from the raw file, rebuilds the normalized counts of the united table from the raw counts (which fixes the library order), and confirms that its pooled differences equal step 05's meth.diff to 1e-8. Independent cross-checks agree: awk on two raw files, a Python reading of the reference, pwilcox and dhyper by hand, and all 176 per-library and 54 per-CpG values of the verifying agent's tables.

Nothing outside `06_diagnostics/locus_nc047563*` was edited. An early snapshot of the script was committed by the parent session (40cd66d, "unreviewed"); the working-tree file is the finished one.

design_decisions: The DML region is read from step 07 (dml_regions_legacy.csv, largest run of ploidy DML), so its coordinates are not typed in. This adds a dependency on step 07 beyond the step 05 tables. The script stops if that run is not on NC_047563.1.
The window is the DML region plus 10 kb on either side (39623323 to 39645520), close to the suggested 39,625,000 to 39,645,000. The script stops if the block and its 5 kb flanks do not fit.

Block rule: a CpG has excess coverage when at least one library is at or above its upper cutoff; such CpGs within 1 kb form a run; the block is the run that holds the DML region. I chose the cutoff because it is the criterion by which corrected mode removes a CpG, not to match the target.

Carrier rule: at least one tested CpG of the region at or above the library's cutoff. Because the Fisher result for cohort depends on the rule, the script also reports a stricter rule (every CpG at the cutoff) and Wilcoxon tests on the size of the excess, on two scales.

Per-library medians over a zone use only the CpG sites with reads in that library, as the library median does. In the per-CpG profile a library without reads counts as 0. Both are stated in the header.
Coverage relative to the cutoff is written per library as a ratio and per CpG as the number of libraries at or above the cutoff, not as a per-CpG ratio.

Leave-one-out applies the difference rule only, as instructed, and the output says each count is therefore the largest possible number of DML. I added one row for the 9 libraries without the excess taken alone.
Wilcoxon tests are exact, with the normal approximation written beside each for part d. The script stops if two libraries tie on percent methylation.

Part f counts all 3,570 30-mers of the block, not only the sample of 60, which is kept for comparison. It also reports where the second copies of the two-copy 30-mers lie and whether any library reaches its cutoff there. The latter costs no second pass: the first pass keeps every position at or above the cutoff.

The summary has four columns (section, quantity, value, how_defined), one more than specified. Values are text: a number, a label, 'x of y' or 'a to b'. Setting values are interpolated into the definitions.
The script calls setDTthreads(1), so the stated run time and memory hold on a shared machine.
The profile carries extra columns: zone, DML flags, step 05's meth.diff for tested CpGs, libraries with reads, and min and max relative coverage per class.
left_out: No model refit in the leave-one-out (the verifying agent used glm with p < 2e-4): left out by instruction.
Share of soft-masked bases in the block (the agent's 10%): not computed, because Biostrings drops letter case and it was not a target.
Relative coverage at the three places that hold second copies: the script reports only whether the cutoff is reached there (it is not), because medians would need a second pass over the 22 files.
Coverage beyond 10 kb either side of the region (the agent looked at 100 kb): not in the script.
README.md and issues.md were not edited, by rule; proposed text is in the caveats and in readme_row.
caveats: The cohort difference in the size of the excess cannot be attributed. Cohort, stock and sequencing batch coincide (I-01, I-08), and control libraries are somewhat higher within both classes, so part of it may be a batch effect on the coverage of this GC-richer block.

'Carries the excess' is a threshold on a continuous quantity. Three heat triploids sit just above it (zr3534_6, _7, _8: 1.04 to 1.22 times the cutoff, 29 to 42 of 54 CpGs), and they are what moves the Fisher p for cohort from 0.19 to 0.012.

The issue's sentence that the heat loci are 'not methylation regulated by heat' is supported for the 22-library analysis: without zr3534_4 the median heat difference is -5.66 points and no CpG passes. Among the 9 libraries without the excess, 24 CpGs still exceed 20 points for heat and 37 for ploidy, with groups of 3 and 6. That reflects the four heat-cohort diploids at 34% to 43% and is description only.
Each library is treated as one animal. The sample sheet names the animal for the heat cohort only (I-36).
Run time was measured with the machine under load (load average about 5). Peak memory varied between 1.45 and 1.53 GB across runs.
The 06_diagnostics README needs the row below and the line `Rscript 06_diagnostics/locus_nc047563.R` in its run list.
An exploration file (explore_window.rds) was written to the repository root by mistake early on and moved to scratch within a minute.

Exploration not in the script, so not reproducible from the repository: within 100 kb either side no CpG outside the block reaches a cutoff, and median coverage at the two larger second-copy places is ordinary in all 22 libraries.

Proposed text for issues.md, I-09, bullet 1: The block of excess coverage is NC_047563.1:39,633,065-39,636,662 (3.6 kb, 82 CpG sites, 56 of them tested, all removed by the filter): the CpGs at which at least one library is at or above its upper cutoff. The 5 kb on either side have ordinary coverage (0.56 to 1.72 times the library median) and no CpG at the cutoff. The ends are those of the cutoff rule; the nearest CpG sites, 182 and 183 bp away, are at 2.5 and 1.3 times the library median in the libraries with the excess.

Proposed text, bullet 2 (replaces 'The excess is not in every animal ... no association with ploidy or cohort'): The excess is in every library and differs in size. All 22 have more coverage in the block than in its flanks (1.3 to 32 times). In 13 the median coverage of the 54 tested CpGs is 10.6 to 35.5 times the library median and reaches the cutoff; in the other 9 it is 2.0 to 5.9 times, with no CpG at the cutoff. The 13 are found in all four groups (4 of 10 heat, 9 of 12 control; 5 of 11 diploid, 8 of 11 triploid). Ploidy shows no difference (Fisher exact p = 0.39; size of the excess, Wilcoxon p = 0.56). Cohort does: the Fisher test on the 13 gives p = 0.19, but with all 54 CpGs required at the cutoff (1 of 10 heat, 8 of 12 control) it gives p = 0.012, and the excess is larger in the control cohort (median 19.9 against 4.4 times the library median, exact Wilcoxon p = 0.009; block over flanks 20.7 against 3.6, p = 0.014). A repeat carried equally by every animal would not give this spread. The pattern is a copy-number difference among individual animals that is larger in the control cohort; cohort, stock and sequencing batch cannot be separated (I-01, I-08).

Proposed text, bullet 3: keep, with 'at most 1 ploidy DML' and add: all 54 CpGs have q < 0.01, so the 20-point rule alone decides; the counts are recomputed differences without a refit; leaving out any other single library leaves 50 to 53 and 29 to 53; zr3534_4 supplies 39% of the heat group's normalized reads. The 9 libraries without the excess alone (6 diploid, 3 triploid; 6 heat, 3 control) still give 37 and 24 CpGs above 20 points.

Proposed text, bullet 4: replace 'Wilcoxon p = 0.007, and p = 0.012 without zr3534_4' by 'exact Wilcoxon p = 0.005, and p = 0.010 without zr3534_4'. The heat cohort (0.008) and control cohort (0.09) values stand.

Proposed text, bullet 5 (replaces 'mostly single-copy'): 69% of the block's 30-mers occur once in the reference (2,471 of 3,570; 42 of 60 in the first sample). 874 occur exactly twice; 474, 294 and 100 of the second copies lie at NC_047560.1:13,874,789-13,881,520, NC_047559.1:4,498,648-4,509,003 and NC_047561.1:36,696,412-36,696,653, where no CpG reaches the cutoff in any library. The last 113 bases of the block occur 11 to 61 times. The block is not in the transposable element track (nearest records 799 bp before and 585 bp after). It lies inside introns of LOC105317102 and LOC105318567, and 3,471 of its 3,599 bases lie in the lncRNA gene LOC105341636, exons and introns at the same coverage (18.9 and 20.5 times the library median), so the extra copies are genomic. GC content is 42.5% against 30.9% and 32.7% in the flanks.
result.readme_row: | `locus_nc047563.R` | What the locus of I-09 is: the largest run of DML of all three legacy lists, on NC_047563.1, whose tested CpGs the upper coverage filter removes. From the 22 raw coverage files, the step 05 and step 07 tables, the feature tracks and the reference: the block of excess coverage around the region and the coverage of its flanks; which libraries carry the excess and how they are spread over ploidy and cohort (Fisher exact tests under two rules, Wilcoxon tests on the size of the excess); how many CpGs still pass the difference threshold when one library at a time is left out (difference rule only, no refit); percent methylation per library by ploidy (exact Wilcoxon tests); genes, exons and transposable elements at the block; GC content, the share of its 30-mers that occur once in the reference, and where the second copies lie. About 2 minutes and 1.5 GB on one core; needs the coverage files and the reference genome in the cache. Issues I-05 and I-09. | `locus_nc047563_summary.csv` (one row per fact, with its definition), `locus_nc047563_per_library.csv`, `locus_nc047563_leave_one_out.csv`, `locus_nc047563_coverage_profile.csv` |

result.summary:
The script is written, runs from the repository root in about 4 minutes (3.7 to 4.1 measured, single thread, peak 1.2 to 1.5 GB), and two consecutive runs of the finished script gave byte-identical CSV files (md5 compared). It reads only step 05 and step 07 tables, the seven tracks and the sample sheet; the raw coverage files are not needed.

What it computes, for both modes, both DML lists and seven tracks (264 rows in feature_odds_matched.csv): (1) odds ratios against all tested and against eligible CpGs, checked in the script against step 07 (all 56 cells equal; the script stops otherwise); (2) Mantel-Haenszel within 5-point methylation bins; (3) within bin and decile of within-group SD; (4) ranges 5-95 and 15-85; (5) transposable elements by coverage quartile; (6) CDS against intron within genes; (7) block-bootstrap intervals (2,000 resamples of 100 kb windows) for 1 (eligible), 2 and 3; (8) for ploidy, 1,000 label permutations within cohort, plus 1,000 that also keep the acute heat shock balanced.

Legacy results, ploidy then heat. Gene body: 7.08 and 6.14 against all tested; 2.52 and 2.20 against eligible; 2.04 and 1.68 within methylation bins; 1.13 (block interval 0.77 to 1.82) and 1.01 (0.76 to 1.36) within bin and SD decile. After matching: CDS 1.25 and 1.17, intron 0.81 and 0.87, transposable element 1.05 and 1.02, intergenic 0.80 and 0.92. Shuffled ploidy labels (within cohort): gene-body odds ratio against eligible CpGs median 2.61 (2.5th to 97.5th percentile 1.41 to 4.47), the real 2.52 reached in 54.7% of permutations; median 742.5 CpGs called per permutation (5th to 95th percentile 532 to 1,376), 13.5% reach 1,038. Corrected mode reads the same (gene body 2.85 to 1.24 for ploidy, 2.02 to 0.94 for heat after matching; permutation median 3.11, real value reached in 66.5%).

One addition beyond the task list, because issues.md changed while I worked (commit 68a8a1b, 07:14, added a fifth row to the second table of I-41 from a scratch run): the script also computes the matched comparison 3 for every shuffled-label list, with the within-group SD and its deciles recomputed for the groups the shuffled labels define. Result (legacy, within cohort): gene body median 1.06 (0.55 to 2.14), real 1.13 reached in 44%; CDS median 1.17 (0.85 to 1.45), real 1.25 reached in 29%. With acute heat shock also balanced: 1.08 (0.58 to 2.33) and 1.17 (0.83 to 1.44), 26%. This reproduces the integration check's 1.10 (0.58 to 2.33), 1.18 (0.87 to 1.46) and 29%. The script therefore now writes all five rows of that table.

q-value rule, counted from the diffmeth tables: for ploidy every CpG above 20 points also has q below 0.01 (1,038 of 1,038 legacy, largest q 0.0046; 952 of 952 corrected, largest q 0.0052), and the script stops if that fails. For heat one CpG of 2,352 fails the q rule in legacy mode (q 0.018), none of 2,273 in corrected mode. Heat rows in both permutation tables carry NA and the sentence that no permutation exists.

Two targets depart, both explained under targets: transposable element in the top coverage quartile for ploidy is 0.21, not 0.20 (the script keeps the one ploidy DML outside the eligible range, as step 07 does); the share of eligible CpGs called at a mean of 10% to 20% is 0.37%, not 0.30% (the 300-permutation run under-sampled labellings with very many calls; issues.md already says 0.3% to 0.4%).

Checks done outside the script (scratch, not reproducible from the repository): the Mantel-Haenszel estimates were recomputed with table() and mantelhaen.test on factors (identical); the block intervals with a slow weighted-table implementation (identical at 200 resamples); 40 permutations per scheme and mode were recomputed without pruning and with table() plus fisher.test (counts and all seven odds ratios identical); 25 permutations per scheme for the matched odds ratios (identical in legacy, within 4e-4 in corrected, one CpG at a decile boundary); the pruning of never-callable CpGs was identical to full evaluation on 40 permutations.

Proposed text for I-41 (second table, legacy; replaces scratch numbers by those of the script): shuffled labels against eligible CpGs, 1,000 permutations within cohort: gene body 2.61 (1.41 to 4.47), CDS 1.56, transposable element 0.44; real gene-body value reached in 55%, real CDS value (1.68) in 31%. Same lists, same matching: gene body 1.06 (0.55 to 2.14), CDS 1.17 (0.85 to 1.45), real 1.25 reached in 29%. Matched row: 1.13 (0.77 to 1.82) and 1.01 (0.76 to 1.36). For I-06: median 742.5 (5th to 95th percentile 532 to 1,376), 13.5% at or above 1,038; with acute heat shock balanced 750 (516 to 1,748), 15.3%. "Status of the pipeline" can now name 06_diagnostics/feature_odds_matched.R as the diagnostic that writes that table.

I ran no git command that changes state; the snapshot commits of the main session picked the files up (the working tree was clean for 06_diagnostics at the end).

targets.comment: The integration check used fixed SD classes and the shock-balanced scheme; the script uses deciles recomputed per labelling. Real gene-body 1.13 is reached in 44% of permutations.

design_decisions: Convention of step 07 kept in every comparison: all DML of a list against the CpGs of the background that are not in the list. DML outside the background stay in the DML row; the notes column counts them (1 for 10-90, 39 and 73 for 15-85 in legacy mode).

Estimators: unstratified odds ratios are the conditional estimates of fisher.test (identical to step 07); stratified ones are the common odds ratio and interval of stats::mantelhaen.test. A vectorised Mantel-Haenszel formula used for the resamples is checked against mantelhaen.test inside the script. No literature is cited, because I could not check the papers.

Strata: 5-point bins closed on the left over 0 to 100; deciles of within-group SD among eligible CpGs (global, not within bin). Strata without a DML, without another CpG, or without variation in the track add nothing; the output gives strata used and DML in them.
Within-group SD: pooled around the four group means (ploidy by cohort), 18 degrees of freedom, one matrix formula used for the real and the shuffled labels.

Block interval: percentile bootstrap, 2,000 resamples of the 100 kb windows that hold a compared CpG (4,399 legacy, 4,348 corrected), the same resamples for every list, track and comparison of a mode; the Fisher conditional estimate is recomputed on each resample. Bootstrap rather than jackknife because the jackknife interval assumes a normal log odds ratio, which fails where one window holds most DML of a track (53 of 65 ploidy DML in lncRNA).

Permutation as specified (within cohort, 5 and 5, 6 and 6), 1,000 draws, the same labellings for both modes. A second scheme (also balanced on acute heat shock, 3 and 3, 2 and 2) is reported beside it, because the verification used it and the real labels are balanced over it. Results barely differ except in the upper tail of the counts.

The 20-point rule is evaluated on cross-multiplied whole numbers, so a difference of exactly 20 is never called through rounding (in scratch, floating-point arithmetic called 9 of 25 such ties in 40 permutations). With the real labels this rule reproduces the step 05 list exactly; the script checks it.

CpGs whose per-library percentages span no more than the threshold are skipped in the permutation loop. This is exact (a pooled percentage is a weighted mean) and was confirmed against full evaluation in scratch; it brings 1,000 permutations from about 75 to about 15 seconds.

Added: comparison 3 for every shuffled-label list, with SD and deciles recomputed for the shuffled groups, to reproduce the fifth row that entered the I-41 table during this task. With the real labels this code path must return comparison 3; the script checks it.
Added: the number of CpGs called when the ploidy labels are exchanged in one cohort only (3,480 legacy, 3,427 corrected), because it explains the largest permutation counts (3,667 and 4,107).
Mean coverage is the mean of the normalized coverage columns of the united table, quartile cut among eligible CpGs, so the raw coverage files are not read.

Outputs: four CSV files, long format, odds ratios rounded to 4 decimals. The required column names are kept; interval_method, estimate_method and four count columns are added. The within-group SD medians go to a fourth file, feature_odds_matched_within_group_sd.csv, which also shows the balance inside each SD decile.
Randomness: set.seed(20261119) before the label draws, set.seed(20261120) before the block resamples of each mode. data.table threads follow config$cores (default 1).
left_out: Nothing of items (a) to (h) is left out.

Recomputing q-values under shuffled labels: not feasible (a model fit at 480,579 CpGs per permutation). The script applies the difference rule only and says so; a count per permutation is an upper bound on what the full rule would call.

Numbers that entered I-41 during the task and are not in the task list: matching with coverage added (1.23, and 1.48 in a regression), the matched odds ratios without the locus of I-09 (1.02, 0.97, 0.99, 0.89), the share of DML by coverage quartile, and the comparison with binomial sampling (18 against 9.8 points). They still rest on scratch runs.
Block intervals for comparisons 4, 5 and 6, p-values, and the list of loci in both DML lists: not asked for.
A label permutation for heat: none exists; the outputs say so.
caveats: The permutation summaries rest on 1,000 random labellings. Standard errors: about 1 to 1.6 points for the shares, about 10 CpGs for the median count, and the 95th percentile of the count moves by 100 or more between samples. Block-interval ends move by a few percent between seeds.

Quantile strata: a CpG at a decile boundary can change side with floating-point details on another platform or BLAS, which could alter a fourth decimal of a matched odds ratio. On this machine two runs are byte-identical.

Observation from scratch work, not reproduced by the script and worth a follow-up under I-02, I-06 and I-07: the upper tail of the permutation counts is made of labellings close to an exchange of ploidy labels in one cohort. In legacy mode the within-cohort ploidy differences correlate at -0.30 across CpGs, and of the 969 CpGs whose difference exceeds 20 points in both cohorts 788 have opposite signs. Diploid heat is the outlying group (about 13,000 CpGs differ by more than 20 points from diploid control and from triploid heat, against 3,349 between the two control groups). With the heat cohort at its real labels, almost any relabelling of the control cohort calls more CpGs than the real labels (median 1,530 against 1,038). The script only writes the count for the exchanged labelling (3,480).

Matching on deciles is coarse in principle, but in scratch the matched gene-body odds ratio was 1.16, 1.13, 1.12, 1.11 for 5, 10, 20, 40 SD groups (heat 1.03, 1.01, 1.00, 1.00), so the result does not hinge on it.

The matched comparison removes the gene-body excess but shuffled-label lists still show a CDS odds ratio of 1.17 after the same matching, so matching does not make the background fully fair; the permutation columns are the reference to read the real values against.
issues.md, the comment in step 07 and dml_eligible() were edited by other sessions while I worked (text only; no input of the script changed). The targets in the task reflect the earlier text.
The header gives a few expected values as comments (1,038 of 1,038; 952 of 952; one of 2,352; 53 of 65). They are not used by the code and would need editing if step 05 changes.

Repeats the odds ratios of step 07 and stops if they differ; then compares DML with eligible CpGs of the same 5-point methylation bin, of the same bin and decile of within-group SD, with other ranges of mean methylation (5% to 95%, 15% to 85%), by coverage quartile (transposable elements) and CDS against intron; adds intervals from a bootstrap over 100 kb blocks. For ploidy, the same odds ratios for CpG lists made with shuffled labels (1,000 permutations within cohort, and 1,000 that also keep the acute heat shock balanced), with the number of CpGs called per permutation. The permutation applies the difference rule only; no permutation exists for heat. Both modes. About 4 minutes, 1.5 GB. Issues I-41 and I-06. | `feature_odds_matched.csv`, `feature_odds_matched_within_group_sd.csv`, `feature_odds_label_permutation.csv`, `feature_odds_label_permutation_counts.csv` |

result.summary:
The script is written, runs from the repository root in 2 to 3 minutes at 1.2 GB, and reproduces every target of parts (a) to (f) exactly. Two consecutive runs of the finished script gave byte-identical CSV files.

Part (g) departs from its target because of the unit of the test totals, not because of an error on either side:
- **As step 09 tests** (totals in lines of the universe map, which is what the task asks for): 555 of 12,720 BP terms have p < 0.01 for the accession-run list, against a median of 47 for 200 random lists of the same size (range 8 to 287).
- **With one entry per transcript** (what the verifying agent ran, as issues.md itself says): 1,041, the target, against a median of 47.5 (range 9 to 256). The script's first ten draws are the agent's ten draws and give its 52.5 (13 to 157).
- Nine of the ten legacy top BP terms are below 0.01 in both units; the exception is GO:0035561.
- The legacy list itself gives 383 terms, with p-values equal to those of step 09.

The script also regenerates the size-matched check that issues.md assigns to it, and this changes one statement there. At the size of the legacy list (612 transcripts), position alone does not raise the number of terms under the totals the legacy test used: median 36 for lists drawn from the run against 43.5 for lists from the whole universe. The "about doubles" of issues.md holds only with transcript totals (81 against 38). The reason is that run transcripts have 2.14 map lines each against 1.79 for the universe, and the line totals count that against a list from the run.

A second small correction: ploidy survivors do not come from five linkage groups only. 608 of the 623 lie on the first five, 9 on four of the other five, and 6 on unplaced scaffolds.

What the script stops on: any of the four reads not returning the rows predicted from the quote rule of scan(); its counts differing from `legacy_reader_loss.csv` or `legacy_funnel.csv`; its legacy p-values differing from `legacy_fisher_ploidy_BP.csv`; or the direct hypergeometric computation used for the random lists not matching topGO bit for bit on the two fixed lists. I confirmed four altered-input cases in scratch copies (an apostrophe removed, a nine-field line, a comment character, a missing table); each stopped with a plain message and wrote no file.

No README, helper, pipeline script, run_config.R or issues.md was edited, and I ran no state-changing git command. The parent session's check-in commits picked up the script and outputs while I worked; `git diff HEAD` is empty for all four files.

design_decisions: The legacy files in 03_input_files/annotation/legacy/ are read, as the task states. The default read is the pipeline's own read_dml_annotation(reader = "legacy"); the three other quote settings use the same read.table call with only `quote` changed.

Which line starts which row is predicted by a small re-implementation of the quote rule of scan() (R sources, src/main/scan.c, fillBuffer(), read in the R 4.1.0 copy the verifying agent saved). The script stops unless each of the four reads of each table returns exactly the predicted rows.

Two scratch cross-checks of that prediction, not part of the script: the line-number wrapping method of the checking agent gave the same structure for all three tables, and 6,000 random small files under four quote settings matched scan() itself with no failure.

Two interventions instead of one: replacing apostrophes on the unpaired lines alone restores every line, and replacing them on all other apostrophe lines changes nothing. The interventions are read from lines in memory, after a check that this route returns what the read of the file returns.

A transcript survives when it is named in the transcript column of a returned row. Accession order is the numeric order of the number in XM_<number>.<version>, so the result does not depend on the collation of the R session.

Linkage groups are also reported as two fixed halves in the order of config$linkage_groups, for all three tables. The reason is computed and reported: the annotated mRNAs in the accession range of the ploidy run lie on the first five and on unplaced scaffolds.
Position control in two units, map lines as step 09 and one entry per transcript, so that both the task's definition and the number in issues.md are reproducible from one file.

The two fixed lists are tested by topGO itself, on two topGO objects. The 600 random lists use the same hypergeometric tail computed from topGO's term members; the script stops unless that computation equals topGO's p-values bit for bit for both fixed lists in both units. One topGO test of a run-sized list takes 27 s, so 600 would not fit the time limit.

200 draws of each of three random kinds, without replacement, set.seed(20261119) with the RNG kinds named; the same lists serve both units. The two kinds at the size of the legacy list were added because issues.md says this script regenerates them.
The ten legacy top terms are taken from legacy_fisher_ploidy_BP.csv of step 09, and the script checks that they are the ten smallest p-values of its own reproduction with no tie at the boundary.

legacy_reader_mechanism.csv keeps the four columns asked for. `value` is text (counts, percentages, yes or no, transcript names, warning texts). Definitions live in one named vector and a quantity without a definition stops the script. Rows under table = "session" record the R, GO.db and topGO versions; rows under "universe" hold facts about the universe.

Additions beyond the task list, all from the Verification paragraph of I-40: survival of transcripts that carry a term with an unpaired apostrophe, the largest merged row, surviving transcripts by linkage-group half, and the apostrophe-only read.
All three files are written at the end, after every check has passed, so a failed run leaves no half-updated set. The main checks carry plain messages.
setDTthreads(1) is set in the script, and R is asked for English messages because warning texts are part of the output.
left_out: Nothing of parts (a) to (g) is left out.
No run under R 4.1.0 or on Windows: only R 4.3.3 is installed. The CSV records the R version that made the reads.

No random lists that keep the isoforms of a gene together. The random lists are single transcripts, so they show what position does and are no null distribution for the 383 terms of the legacy list. The header says so; such a control belongs with I-03 and I-41.
The position control covers the BP test of the ploidy table only, as asked; no CC or MF, no heat or shared.
No per-draw table: the control file holds median, minimum, 5th and 95th percentile and maximum per kind of list.
No README, issues.md or pipeline file was edited; proposed text is under caveats and in readme_row.
caveats: The 1,041 of issues.md and the 555 of this script answer different questions. 555 is the test as step 09 runs it; 1,041 is the same list with one entry per transcript. Quote either with its unit.
Counts for random lists vary widely (8 to 287 terms for run-sized lists), so a median from ten draws (52.5) and one from 200 (47.5) differ without contradiction.

Proposed text for issues.md I-40, first sentence of the linkage-group bullet: "For ploidy 608 of the 623 surviving transcripts lie on five of the ten linkage groups (9 lie on four of the other five, 6 on unplaced scaffolds)."

Proposed text for issues.md I-40, the position bullet: "How much that skew matters was tested, with limits (`06_diagnostics/legacy_reader_mechanism.R`, `legacy_reader_position_control.csv`). With every universe transcript of the accession run as the list of interest (11,284 of the 27,469 transcripts, no DML information) and the test as step 09 runs it, 555 of the 12,720 BP terms have p < 0.01, against a median of 47 for 200 random lists of the same size (range 8 to 287). With one entry per transcript in place of the line totals of the legacy test (I-43) the numbers are 1,041 and 47.5 (range 9 to 256). Nine of the ten legacy top BP terms for ploidy are below 0.01 either way (all but GO:0035561). That list is 18 times as long as the legacy list of 612 transcripts. At the length of the legacy list position alone does not raise the number under the totals the legacy test used: 200 random lists of 612 transcripts drawn from the run give a median of 36 BP terms with p < 0.01 (range 2 to 191), against 43.5 for lists drawn from the whole universe (4 to 237). The transcripts of the run have more map lines each (2.14 against 1.79 for the universe), and the line totals count that against a list from the run. With one entry per transcript position about doubles the number (medians 81 and 38). In 175 of the 200 lists from the run (171 with transcript totals) none of the ten legacy top terms has p < 0.01, and the legacy list itself gives 383 terms (638 with transcript totals). Position therefore does not explain the legacy top terms, which is the isoform count of I-03; the random lists are lists of single transcripts and are no null distribution for a list of isoform sets."
The request for English messages could not be tested in a non-English locale: only C and C.utf8 are installed here, and R does not translate messages in either.
The script needs the committed outputs of steps 08 and 09 and GO.db 3.13.0 in the cache. use_legacy_go_db() downloads the package if it is absent, as step 09 does.

The three tables also hold lines with an empty GO term and an ontology letter of "None" or empty (59, 166 and 10 lines). They do not affect any count here, but a plain strsplit drops the empty last field, which the script handles.

For heat and shared the longest surviving run is reported for completeness but is not a meaningful summary: heat survivors form 13 runs and the longest holds 57% of them; in shared every transcript survives.
The parent session's check-in commits picked up the script and the three CSV files while I worked. HEAD (454bf25) holds the final versions. I ran no state-changing git command.

Scratch work, including the four altered-input test copies, is in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-WGBS-gigas-ploidy-desiccation/ed665b6a-3457-5aca-a521-7838dbc31cfa/scratchpad/wf/build-legacy_reader_mechanism. A safety check refused an rm there, so nothing was deleted.
result.readme_row: | `legacy_reader_mechanism.R` | How the legacy enrichment script lost most of the ploidy annotation table and a quarter of the heat table: `read.table()` with its default quote characters, and apostrophes in GO term names. For the three legacy tables: rows, transcripts and genes returned by four reads (default quote characters, no quote character, the double quote alone, the apostrophe alone) with the warnings R gives; the lines with an unpaired apostrophe, the merged rows, and the proof by intervention; the transcripts and genes that vanish; where the survivors lie (accession run, linkage groups); the overlap with the universe gap; survival by number of transcripts per gene. For ploidy, a position-only control of the BP test: every universe transcript of the surviving accession run as the list of interest, against 200 seeded random lists of each of three kinds, with the totals counted in map lines (as step 09) and in transcripts. Stops unless every read returns the rows predicted from the quote rule of `scan()` and its counts and p-values equal those of step 09. 2 to 3 minutes, about 1.2 GB; needs the outputs of steps 08 and 09 and GO.db 3.13.0 in the cache. Issues I-40, I-39, I-43. | `legacy_reader_mechanism.csv` (long format: table, quantity, value, definition), `legacy_reader_by_linkage_group.csv`, `legacy_reader_position_control.csv` |
